chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the owned slave is blinded, there is no slavery upon him; and the slave, when he suffers from leprosy, there is no slavery upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the physical conditions that lead to the emancipation of a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'iklāl' (incapacitation) as a ground for automatic emancipation, reflecting the Shia juristic view that specific physical ailments like blindness or leprosy render the slave unable to fulfill their duties, thus warranting freedom. It highlights the merciful dimension of Islamic manumission laws, where the master bears the cost of the slave's disability as a form of compensation for their service. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the rights of slaves and the conditions under which slavery is dissolved without requiring a separate manumission deed.
